rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Given explicit method descriptors, argument specializers/type evidence, class precedence lists and the generic function's argument-precedence-order, return the deterministic most-specific-first ordered list of applicable methods without invoking any method. Use the ratified precedence rules; registration order is not a semantic tie-breaker, and do not invent ambiguity when class/argument precedence resolves the order.
rows.falsifier: Hold method identities, applicability, class precedence lists and argument-precedence-order fixed while permuting registration order: the query order must remain identical. Include a two-argument case where the first argument's specializer ranking conflicts with the second so an explicit argument-precedence-order determines the winner. Assert no method body or side effect runs during the query. Any ambiguity claim when that precedence law orders the methods is a failed witness.
rows.distinct_from_existing: DEFMETHOD and DEFGENERIC already selected: distinguish query/ordering from definition

rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Inside an admitted effective-method context return exact D1 yes/no for whether another applicable method exists
rows.falsifier: At last primary method answer D1 NO; outside a method context BLOCK rather than truthy NIL
rows.distinct_from_existing: No new D1 resident; D10 library predicate returns the existing D1 value

rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Delegate to the next ordered method preserving or explicitly replacing arguments under established method-combination semantics
rows.falsifier: Invoking at end or outside dynamic method context must signal defined error, never fall back to guessed function identity
rows.distinct_from_existing: Invocation sequencing may belong to D2 sole language-control owner; do not ratify D10 as new control syntax

rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Construct, without invoking methods, a normalized effective-method plan from applicable methods using standard combination order: around methods most-specific-first; before methods most-specific-first; primary methods most-specific-first; after methods least-specific-first. Include a defined fail-closed outcome when the standard combination requires a primary method but none applies.
rows.falsifier: For the same method set, qualifiers, specializers, class precedence lists and argument-precedence-order, permutations of registration order must yield the same normalized plan. Verify the reversed order of after methods, most-specific-first order for before/primary/around, and the missing-primary failure. Plan construction itself must not execute method bodies.
rows.distinct_from_existing: Compare existing DEFGENERIC/DEFMETHOD and ordinary CONS/LIST as representation, not equivalent precedence semantics

rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Represent failure of explicit message dispatch when no applicable method is available, keeping object/message identity in data
rows.falsifier: A method-not-found case must not invent an execution result or silently select another method
rows.distinct_from_existing: Possibly merely an existing explicit error result; require independent observable law before D10 slot

rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Present a first-class condition value to an explicitly supplied lexical handler chain without turning it into host I/O
rows.falsifier: Unmatched condition must remain available as typed failure with unmodified payload; no implicit host exception
rows.distinct_from_existing: Signaling/handler control likely belongs to D2 or effect ledger rather than D10 new structural control

rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Purely find a named restart in the current dynamic environment; when a condition is supplied, include restarts explicitly associated with that condition and restarts associated with no condition, excluding those associated only with other conditions. For duplicate names, return the innermost (most recently established) applicable restart. Return the restart descriptor or NIL/absence; never invoke it.
rows.falsifier: Positive: an inner same-name restart shadows the outer; an unassociated restart remains findable when a condition is supplied; a restart associated only with a different condition is excluded. Negative: once its dynamic extent ends, the restart is absent. The query must not transfer control or mutate state. A merely lexical lookup or a query that invokes the restart fails.
rows.distinct_from_existing: Not equal to already-selected historical UNDO/INTERLISP-HISTORY-REPLAY, which concern historical state

rows.historical_provenance: Source is the historical design reference, NOT an existing SENS implementation
rows.semantic_law: Invoke a selected restart with exact supplied arguments, with scope and continuation preserved
rows.falsifier: Invoking stale/out-of-scope restart BLOCK; no default branch or OS capability is inferred
rows.distinct_from_existing: Nonlocal transfer is control; D2 owns language control; owner must approve a pure functional encoding
